relations.subject: Jan Gonda
relations.evidence: he obtained the chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University in 1932 as the indirect successor of Caland (after a short interregnum of Rahder who became a Japanologist).

relations.subject: Jan Gonda
relations.evidence: during which he attended Caland's classes on Sanskrit and related subjects

relations.subject: Jan Gonda
relations.evidence: he wrote a thesis on the Indo-European root deik-, guided by the Grecian Vollgraff, and obtained his doctorate at the beginning of 1929.

relations.subject: Jan Gonda
relations.evidence: Then he studied Indonesian linguistics and Old Javanese at Leiden University over a number of years.

relations.subject: Jan Gonda
relations.role: chair of Malay and Javanese Linguistics and Literature
relations.evidence: and he also held the chair of Malay and Javanese Linguistics and Literature from 1932 to 1950.

relations.subject: Jan Gonda
relations.evidence: Gonda, now concentrating more on India, established the Institute of Oriental Languages which became famous for its Department of Indology.
